layout.description: Blank lines, compact getters and readonly sorting fields versus private fields/getters differ. They are not wire behavior; every byte remains snapshot-gated rather than formatting-normalized.

imports.description: TypeScript marks type-only imports explicitly and orders/merges imports differently. This supports verbatimModuleSyntax without changing runtime constructors. .NET output needs normal type-import elision.

command-suppression.description: The .NET command hook contains a ts-ignore comment. TypeScript does not need that suppression with the pinned browser client; both public signatures are checked independently.

query-source.description: The .NET provenance source identifies the read-model type; TypeScript identifies the query method as well. Only the timestamp is variable-normalized; source and body hash remain gated.

sorting.description: .NET 22.45.0 model-bound queries incorrectly emit sortBy.id from the query input rather than the response model. TypeScript's name/detail/notice/status helpers follow the documented read-model-field contract, as does .NET controller-based generation. The browser client sends the field unchanged; id is not a Listing field and fails on .NET IQueryable. This is a .NET defect, not an intentional API difference.

complex-sorting.description: The .NET controller-based generator still emits helpers for complex result fields, which throw on .NET IQueryable; its model-bound snapshot's query-parameter defect masks that limitation. TypeScript retains detail/notice helpers for compatibility but deprecates them for removal in the next major release (https://github.com/Cratis/Arc.TypeScript/blob/main/decisions/0004-defer-generated-proxy-removals-to-the-next-major-release.md), and rejects in-memory sorting on these complex fields with the existing malformedRequest validation result. Database providers retain their own ordering; scalar helpers are unchanged.

enum-names.description: .NET camel-cases enum members to draft/published. TypeScript preserves source names Draft/Published. Numeric wire values 0/1 and numeric hydration agree, so changing source names would be an unnecessary API break.

barrel-ownership.description: TypeScript marks the barrel with a provenance/body-hash header for safe owned-file regeneration. The .NET barrel is unmarked. Exports are identical; destructive .NET cleanup is not adopted.
